_note: Cited public values for the Eady problem; our own numbers are computed, never typed. See SOURCES.md.

eady_cutoff_wavenumber_rounded.how_obtained: read in the lecture-note PDF (pages 7 and 8); two digits only, so the tolerance is half a unit of the last digit
eady_cutoff_wavenumber_rounded.source: Emanuel, MIT OCW 12.803 Lecture 19, text after Eq. (19.17) and under Figure 19.2
eady_cutoff_wavenumber_rounded.what: non-dimensional wavenumber beyond which Eady waves are neutral, as rounded by the source

eady_fastest_wavenumber.source: Emanuel, MIT OCW 12.803 Lecture 19, text after Eq. (19.17): extremum at r = 1.606
eady_fastest_wavenumber.what: non-dimensional wavenumber (N H K / f) of the fastest-growing Eady wave

eady_max_growth_coefficient.how_obtained: read in the lecture-note PDF (page 7) and on the NCL documentation page
eady_max_growth_coefficient.second_source: NCAR Command Language, function eady_growth_rate (coefficient 0.3098; cites Eady 1949, Tellus 1, 33-52, doi:10.1111/j.2153-3490.1949.tb01265.x, and Lindzen & Farrell 1980, J. Atmos. Sci. 37, 1648-1654)
eady_max_growth_coefficient.source: K. A. Emanuel, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.803 Quasi-Balanced Circulations in Oceans and Atmospheres (Fall 2009), Lecture 19 'Baroclinic Instability', text after Eq. (19.17): r c_i = 0.3098
eady_max_growth_coefficient.what: largest growth rate of the Eady wave in units of f (dU/dz) / N (l = 0)
